t: I Fell in Love to Embrace
b: "Give us your mandate to protect democracy," came a quavering voice from the TV
Rahul, at the peak of frustration, shouted from inside his room: "Are you going to turn that TV off now?..... Or shall I just close my book?"
"Wait a bit. Looks like an election is coming. Everyone's started talking. If there's an election they won't put a curfew on. They'll open the campus too," Kalyani replied

"The way things are going, it looks like they won't open the campus this year at all. If they'd just say so, at least I could close my books too. These idiots have kept us stuck halfway, neither one thing nor the other"
"Today's Friday, isn't it. Go and study a while. By tonight they'll say what's happening ..there's only one more exam, isn't there. So what??"

"Do you know how hard that one exam is?" Rahul opened his mouth to moan, then slowly shut it. She wasn't going to understand however he explained. Better to nod quietly and go, he thought, and made only a sound: "Mmm..."
As Rahul opened the door to go into his room,
"Rahul, I forgot to tell you. There are no onions in the house .....!" said Kalyani
"So?"
"Order them from that shop on the phone!"
For a second something seemed to drill into Rahul's head. He went right to the peak of anger.
"Couldn't you have told me to order them yesterday? If I tell him today, will he come for one item?? This is exactly why I told you to order things yourself without asking me ....."
Kalyani's face shrank at once. He was her only child, after all! The words stung her.
"When I phone him, he says to WhatsApp him or something. What do I know about that?" she answered innocently.
"All right! All right! Next time tell me everything at once!" said Rahul, looking at his phone, and slammed his door shut.

Once inside, he looked up and around his room. Hadn't he lived in this hut for three months? Its beauty showed in the sight. Even his meals came to the room. That's how pampered he was. Even the window was shut with a curtain. Rahul's pale skin and the flab newly appeared at his waist showed it had been a long time since he had seen sunlight.

Books and papers lay scattered over the desk. One or two were under the desk too. Rahul took no notice. Beside them, a laptop. Something was playing on it by itself. An English film, it seemed.. Subtitles appeared below in large letters.

His hostel clothes lay strewn over the bed. Only one corner was clean, with nothing on it. Rahul flung himself straight onto it. Lying there, staring at the ceiling, he picked up his phone. The blue light fell on his face. As usual he circled the social media, Facebook, WhatsApp. Suddenly, as if he had thought of something, he tossed the phone onto the bed. It rolled away and found a place of its own.

He understood very well that he needn't have spoken to his mother like that. It's only an onion, he could have kept quiet. That's how he would once have been. That was the real Rahul. But he had lost that Rahul long ago. These days his mind never stayed steady. Some anger, worry and fear had taken him over. He didn't know whom to show it to. Today it came out on Kalyani

But Kalyani would forget all this. Or she would act as though she had forgotten. He couldn't do that. Guilt rose high in him. He knew what he had done was wrong. One word to Amma would be enough. Everything would be fine. But he couldn't manage even that.

He must have thought of studying again. He went to the desk and picked up a book. A few minutes would have passed. He closed it. How many times can you read the same thing over and over, he consoled himself. There was just one exam left. Once it was over, he would be a graduate. But corona had got there first. The dream of graduating became the horizon. Was that the only dream corona had played with?

Somehow Rahul got the phone he had thrown back into his hands. Suji's photo peeped out. Suji had studied with him. He sighed with longing, wishing he could just stay by her side. What use was longing? Is longing alone enough? What fruit do words never spoken bear? Three years of seeing her, talking, spending time together, and he still didn't have the courage to tell her he loved her; what could he do? All his courage came out only when he spoke to his mother, didn't it

To put a full stop to it all.. that is, as the first point of his love, he decided to tell her in person when the final exam was over. Just when he found the courage, corona did what it does. Before he could speak, Sujitha had left for her home town

Rahul didn't know whether to laugh or cry. Even poems and music, which usually soothed him, only added to his pain these days. When he thought of something he had read somewhere, that unspoken love holds more sweetness, only anger came. Rahul was afraid of what her answer would be if he told her. But what if he never got to tell her at all?

Every week, more than the thought that if the campus opened the exam would be over, the hope that he could see Suji and tell her of his love rose highest in him. Meanwhile another fear had caught hold of him. For many of his girl friends, their families had already started talking about marriage. What if Sujitha's family too had started something like that? What could he possibly do? He prayed that nothing like that would happen
There was a noise outside. Rahul peeped out. Kalyani was searching for something
"What is it, Amma? What's the matter?" he asked gently. He was trying to forget that he had shouted at his mother a little earlier. Kalyani didn't seem to remember it
"The milkman has come outside."
"Oh.... money? It's right here on the table!"

"Not that ................that mask!........ I washed it only yesterday and put it away. Where has it gone ...ah............here it is!!!!!" and hurriedly putting on the face mask she had found, Kalyani went out.

Rahul felt like laughing. Three months ago, if he had even dreamed that things would come to this, it would have been a joke. But now?? For a second Rahul thought that Sujitha too must now go out with her face covered. At once a poem of Bharathiyar's came to mind.
"It was the custom of the Turks of Delhi, my girl! – for women
to veil and hide the flower of their face;
The art of love is not learned by being told – is there
any love here that hides the light of the face?"

'Did Bharathi write it just for her? But a face mask would suit her better than a veil. Isn't the source of her beauty those eyes!..Che. Is it right to think like this about a girl who isn't yet mine? No, no. She is the one who is going to be mine!! All this time, could she not have had feelings for me too? Or could she have failed to understand that there was something in my heart? Surely not!! She is waiting until I tell her. That's how it must be.'
He talked to the screen of his own mind

Rahul wondered what Sujitha would be doing now..What doubt was there, she'd surely be studying. 'She said her father runs a shop. Won't this corona have stopped his business?'.....Poor Mama!' he thought, and smiled without realising it. 'I haven't even told her I love her yet. And already it's Mama and Mami, family,' he must have thought.
"Rahul! Rahul!" he heard Kalyani calling
"What, Amma?" he asked
"Breaking news is on. Come and see!"
Rahul hurried out.
"The curfew is being relaxed across the country. Universities will reopen next week for final-year students only"
"With the elders' consent we will do the wedding rites later;
would I wait, my girl? Here, take a kiss on the cheek...." Rahul's lips murmured without his knowing.
note: The title and the closing lines come from Subramania Bharathi's love poems to Kannamma; the veil verse is Bharathi's too. Mama and Mami: the words for a father- and mother-in-law.
